card.name: Padayani
card.tagline: Kerala Bhadrakali temple ritual of painted kolams
card.profile: Padayani (Padeni) is a ritual folk art of Bhadrakali (Bhagavati) temples of Central Travancore, Kerala, commemorating the dance performed to pacify goddess Kali's rage after she slew the demon Darika (Kerala Tourism). Its hallmark is the kolam - large masks/effigies painted on arecanut palm spathes in natural pigments (green, carbon-black, turmeric-yellow, vermilion) representing figures such as Bhairavi, Kalan (death), Yakshi and Pakshi. Evolving from the healing ritual Kolam Thullal, it involves the Kaniyar (Ganaka) community for lyrics and costume and Nair performers, with percussion on the patayani thappu, chenda and para. It is performed from roughly mid-December to mid-May at temples like Kadammanitta (G. Venu, Natana Kairali).
card.insight: Padayani is distinct from Theyyam: it is centred on Bhadrakali temple festivals of southern/central Kerala and on impermanent areca-spathe kolams, whereas Theyyam belongs to North Malabar and embodies deities directly (Kerala Tourism).
